title: Minister of State Smt. Savitri Thakur Celebrates 10 Years of UPI, Says Phone Has Become the Wallet of Every Indian
body_text:
Minister of State for Women and Child Development, Smt. Savitri Thakur celebrated the completion of 10 years of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI).
In a post on 'X' the Union Minister of State said that there was a time when carrying cash was a must, while today, phone has become the wallet. She said that from chai stalls to college canteens, and from villages to big businesses, UPI has made payments remarkably simple – a few taps, a few seconds and zero hassle.
She said that this ease and speed of digital payments reflects the India that is being built today.

ministry.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development

enrichment.summary: MoS for Women and Child Development Savitri Thakur marked 10 years of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) with a social media post praising its role in simplifying digital payments across India. She noted that UPI has replaced cash for transactions ranging from small vendors to large businesses, calling the phone the modern 'wallet'.
enrichment.context: UPI, launched by NPCI in 2016, has become the backbone of India's digital payments ecosystem, processing billions of transactions monthly and being cited internationally as a model for real-time payment systems. Its growth is often linked to the broader Digital India and financial inclusion agenda, including Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity initiatives. However, this particular release is a ministerial social media commentary celebrating an anniversary rather than announcing any new policy, data, or scheme related to UPI or the Ministry of Women and Child Development's mandate.
